banner: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Change fictional CORS policy between versions, preserve both existing origins with a compatible candidate, and observe an incompatible candidate's native browser denial without bypass.
sourceRequiredBehavior: Preserve browser access for existing origins throughout migration.
sourceAcceptance: Real browser enforcement is measured; valid existing origins continue, and denied access is not bypassed for the demo.
preconditions: Open index.html directly for a teaching-only expectation; actual CORS and user impact stay unknown.
For actual origin observations run node learning\S107\serve.cjs and open BOTH printed HTTP frontend URLs.
The operator owns all three listeners, which bind only literal 127.0.0.1 at actual ephemeral ports for at most 15 minutes.
Automated verification needs existing approved Node 22.23.4, public Microsoft Playwright 1.56.1 cached distributions and installed signed Edge 156.0.4314.50.
actions: Predict baseline v1 reading from both A and B and send their actual browser cross-origin API requests.
Select compatible v2 on both origins and observe preserved reading.
Select incompatible v2: A reads, B is CORS-denied despite a finished HTTP 200 response.
Recover B with compatible v2; its original interrupted attempt remains in the journal.
Inspect separate education verifier, user impact, browser assessment and metadata-only receipt.
Exercise a wrong prediction and missing observation; reset controls without deleting attempts.

syntheticInput.profile: Fictional Cedar learner; no real business data
syntheticInput.receiptCorrelation: A per-document non-secret UUID matches each current HTTP receipt. It is instrumentation, not authentication, identity or a credential.
syntheticInput.historyEviction: None; reset retains all attempts. Reload ends the in-memory client journal but does not remove the server ledger.

expectedAssertions: Compatible migration preserves actual browser reading for both pre-existing origins.
Incompatible B access has matching actual Origin/finished HTTP 200/no allow-origin receipt and Chromium's native CORS diagnostic.
No denied payload is made available through same-origin receipts, routing, a proxy or altered browser security.
Missing receipts, unchecked payloads, CSP denials and generic network errors remain unknown.
An older document's real denied HTTP 200 receipt cannot qualify a new document's network failure; original receipts remain retained.
Static predictions and model flags never have empirical certification authority.
Original failed, interrupted and unknown attempts survive later success and reset; attempt seven is refused.
Real DOM keyboard controls, invalid-input error, reset, network failure and restrictive CSP are checked.
Normal verification changes no bundle or historical evidence bytes.
limits: All application policies, versions and data are fictional, even though native browser CORS enforcement is real.
No arbitrary URLs, external requests, cookies, credentials, system/DNS/TLS changes, cloud calls, identity, configuration, deployment or spending.
No packages/framework installation, download, private extension copy, root/shared-helper edit or unsafe browser security flag.
The shared published same-origin buffered helper cannot qualify this protocol; the test-only native launcher is entirely within S107.
Caller-owned documents use exact-origin CSP and a fixed asset/action allowlist; this is not an OS-level network sandbox.
Only this local browser pair is observed; no arbitrary browser, Azure, production Node 24, source-parent or five-nines certification.
iac: N/A — local fictional browser lesson and owned ephemeral Node HTTP fixture only

verification.normalVerification: Read-only; exact CAPTURE_BROWSER_EVIDENCE=1 deliberately captures new immutable observations, including failures.
verification.empiricalAuthority: Successful browser-native-*.json plus matching byte-exact raw report and input snapshots, not this manifest or a model flag.
